howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co., to activate your license and start working.

Flagler Beach is a quiet, sought-after coastal town in Flagler County, the sixth-fastest-growing county in Florida. Here's exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in Flagler Beach?

You earn the Florida real estate sales associate license, valid statewide. There is no separate Flagler Beach license. Be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is Flagler Beach a good market for a new real estate agent?

Yes. It pairs coastal desirability with county-wide growth. Flagler Beach itself is a smaller, sought-after beach town, while surrounding Flagler County is the sixth-fastest-growing county in Florida, adding about 25,000 residents between 2020 and 2025. That combination, premium coastal property plus a rising tide of new residents, gives a new agent both higher-value deals and steady demand to work.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. A recognized local name carries real weight, and sellers trust it before you say a word.

Why start your real estate career with Adams, Cameron & Co.?

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been the area's largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents and offices across Volusia and Flagler County. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network.

What is your next step?

Read the licensing guide, then start a conversation with Adams, Cameron & Co. No pressure, just a clear picture of the path.
